High Court Of Judicature At Allahabad

sentences.text:
?Neutral Citation No. - 2024:Ahc:176241
Court No. - 66
Case :- Criminal Misc. Bail Application No. - 38831 of 2024

Applicant :- Hridesh @ Monu Dwivedi
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.

Counsel for Applicant :- Suresh Yadav
Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.
Hon'ble Sameer Jain,J.
1.

Heard Sri Yogendra Singh Advocate holding brief of Sri Suresh Yadav, learned counsel for the
applicant and Sri Imran Khan, learned Aga-I for the State-respondent.

2.  The instant application has been filed seeking release of the applicant on bail in Case Crime No.
97 of 2024, under Sections 498A, 323, 304B IPC and 3/4 D.P. Act, Police Station Kadaura, District Jalaun, during pendency of the trial in the court below.

3. FIR of the present case was lodged against applicant and his family members and according to the FIR, marriage of the applicant was solemnized with the daughter of the informant on 25.6.2019 and after marriage applicant and his family members tortured her for additional demand of Rs. 1.5 lacs and in this regard a panchayat was also held but behavior of the applicant and his family members could not be changed.

4. It is further mentioned in the FIR that on 13.6.2024 informant received an information that after making assault, applicant and his family members threw his daughter in the well and thereafter Hridesh @ Monu Dwivedi vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5628673/

sentences.text:
when informant arrived at spot then dead body of the daughter was removed from the well and post mortem was conducted.
5.

Learned counsel for the applicant submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and on the basis of false allegation of demand of dowry and torture, he has been made accused in the present matter.
6.

He further submitted that actually deceased resided in her matrimonial home alongwith her husband i.e. applicant and mother in law and she did not want to live with her mother in law and always insisted her husband i.e. applicant to live separately but when applicant refused for the same then she committed suicide by making jump into the well.

7. He further submitted that however, post mortem report of the deceased suggests that deceased died due to ante mortem injuries and she sustained four ante mortem injuries but it reflects that when she jumped into the well then she sustained these ante mortem injuries and due to these injuries she died and therefore, it cannot be said that it is not a case of suicidal death.
8. He further submitted that applicant is having no criminal history and he is in jail in the present matter since 16.6.2024.

9. Per contra, learned AGA opposed the prayer for bail and submitted that applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry.
10.

He further submitted that from the post mortem report it appears that deceased sustained two contusions and one abrasion and one crushed injury and as per autopsy surgeon, she died due to ante mortem injuries and applicant did not properly explain the death of his wife and neither he can explain the injuries sustained by her.
11.

He further pointed out that in para-27 of the affidavit filed in support to the instant bail application, applicant made an averment which is not only vague but also contrary and therefore,
considering the entire facts of the case, applicant should not be released on bail.
12. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

13. Applicant is husband of the deceased and his wife died within seven years of her marriage in her matrimonial home under abnormal circumstances and there is also allegation of demand of dowry and however, learned counsel for the applicant submitted that deceased committed suicide by making jump into the well but in paragraph 27 of the affidavit, he made an averment that accidentally, deceased fell into the well and therefore, there are material contradictions in the arguments advanced by learned counsel for the applicant and the averment made by the applicant in the instant bail application.

Hridesh @ Monu Dwivedi vs State Of U.P. on 11 November, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/5628673/

sentences.text: Further, from the post mortem report it reflects that deceased sustained two contusions, one abrasion and one crushed injury and how she sustained crushed injury has not been explained by the applicant in the instant bail application and even as per the post mortem report, she died due to ante mortem injuries and therefore, at this stage, allegations levelled against the applicant that after making assault, applicant and his family members threw the deceased in the well, cannot be completely, brushed aside, at this stage.
15. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case, discussed above, I am not inclined to release the applicant on bail.
16. Accordingly, the instant bail application stands rejected.

17. It is clarified that the observations made herein are limited to the facts brought in by the parties pertaining to the disposal of bail application and the said observations shall have no bearing on the merits of the case during trial.
